Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat Muhammad

It is a Medinan surah. This surah is also called Surat al-Qital (the Chapter of Fighting), and Surat al-Anfal is called Surat al-Jihad (the Chapter of Striving). When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah fought the non-Arabs and others after the Messenger of Allah, they would recite these two surahs between the two battle lines, in order to incite the Muslims to fight.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar from the way of Allah, He will render their deeds void.﴾ That is: He will nullify their deeds. The exegetes said: The verse was revealed concerning the feeders on the day of Badr, who were twelve men, each of whom slaughtered ten camels every day. This is the well-known opinion. And ﴿their deeds﴾ refers to their feeding, which Allah, the Exalted, nullified and did not accept from them. It is also said: the verse refers to all the disbelievers of Mecca.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 2:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds and believed in what was sent down upon Muhammad﴾. The well-known view regarding this verse is that it refers to the Ansar (the Helpers of Medina). It was also said that it refers to all who believed alongside the Prophet.

His saying: ﴿And it is the truth from their Lord﴾, meaning: they believed in what is the truth from their Lord.

His saying: ﴿He will remove from them their misdeeds and set right their state﴾, meaning: their condition. It is said: "ma balaka" and "ma haluka" carry the same meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 3:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood⦈. That is: that which We did, namely the nullifying (iḥbāṭ) of the deeds of the disbelievers, and the acceptance of the deeds of the believers, the expiation of their misdeeds, and the setting right of their condition, was because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, and because those who believed followed the truth from their Lord.

And His saying: ﴿Thus Allah sets forth examples for the people⦈. That is: examples of the misdeeds of the disbelievers and the good deeds of the believers. It is said: "I struck a parable for so-and-so" (ḍarabtu lifulān mathalan), meaning: I related to him a kind of speech for a known meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, then strike necks﴾, meaning: strike the necks. "Striking the necks" means cutting them off and severing them.

In the tafsir (exegesis) it is related that some Muslims whom the Prophet had sent to fight a people among the disbelievers burned some of the disbelievers. The Prophet learned of this and disapproved of it, and said: "I was not sent to punish anyone with the punishment of God." Then God, exalted is He, revealed this verse and taught them the manner of killing.

His saying: ﴿until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them﴾. Al-ithkhan (inflicting slaughter) means reaching the utmost limit in inflicting harm. It is also said: it means increasing the killing.

His saying: ﴿then bind them firmly﴾, meaning: take them captive and bind them. Al-Awza'i was asked how one should bind a captive. He said: with a rope. It was asked: is it binding with a leather thong? He said: that is severe. It was said to him: and binding a woman? He said: yes.

His saying: ﴿then either release them as a favour or ransom them﴾. Regarding this verse there are several opinions. The first: it is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated), and this is the well-known view. Mujahid and others said: the imam has the choice regarding the captives: if he wishes he may kill, if he wishes he may ransom, if he wishes he may release them as a favour, and if he wishes he may enslave them. This is also transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas. What we have mentioned is the view of al-Shafi'i and many of the imams.

The second opinion: the verse is abrogated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. This was said by Qatada, al-Suddi and others.

﴿Had God willed, He would have avenged Himself upon them, but that He may test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the way of God—He will not let their deeds go astray﴾.

The third opinion: the verse abrogates His saying: ﴿Then kill the polytheists﴾. This was mentioned by al-Dahhak, and killing is not permissible for captives. The first of these opinions is the most correct, because it has been established by many reports that the Prophet ransomed many captives and released many captives as a favour, as mentioned in the sound books.

His saying: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾. Qatada said: until none remain except a Muslim or one under covenant. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: until 'Isa [son of Maryam] descends from the heaven, breaks the cross, and every disbeliever becomes Muslim. It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A group of my community will continue to fight for the truth until the Hour comes." In another narration: "until the last of them fights the Dajjal." In sum, the war does not lay down its burdens so long as there remains in the world a disbelieving combatant.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That [is so]. And had God willed, He would have avenged Himself upon them﴾, meaning: He would have taken vengeance upon them through a host of angels, or through whatever host He willed. Intiqam (avenging) here means retribution. Its meaning is: had He willed, He would not have commanded you to fight the disbelievers, and would have taken vengeance upon them Himself. ﴿But that He may test some of you by means of others﴾, meaning: that He may test the Muslims by means of the disbelievers, and the disbelievers by means of the Muslims, sometimes victory being for the believers and sometimes for the disbelievers, as happened at Badr and Uhud. This is God's testing, as He wills, of whom He wills.

His saying: ﴿And those who are killed in the way of God﴾, meaning: the martyrs.

His saying: ﴿He will not let their deeds go astray﴾, meaning: He will reward them for their deeds.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿He will guide them and set right their affairs﴾, that is: their condition.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 6:

As for His words: ﴿And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾. The well-known view is that its meaning is: He has made known to them their dwellings. The meaning of His words ﴿which He has made known to them﴾ is: He has clarified it for them, so they will be more guided to their dwellings than people who return from the Friday prayer to their homes. Salamah ibn Kuhayl said: "He made them know (the paths to) their dwellings in Paradise." It is also said: "He made it known to them" means: He made it fragrant for them, and al-'Arf is the scent. In a report: "Whoever helped in the killing of his brother even with half a word will not find the scent (ʿarf) of Paradise, and its scent is found from a distance of five hundred years." This view is related from Ibn 'Abbas. And it is related from Muqatil that he said: When the believer is gathered and ordered to Paradise, the angel who used to record his deeds will precede him and walk with him through Paradise, showing him his dwellings, until, when he reaches the farthest of his dwellings and has seen all of them, the angel departs and leaves the believer in his palaces to enjoy them as he wishes, with whatever he wishes.

And it is related from Mujahid that he said: The believer does not need a guide to his palaces and dwellings; rather he will know them just as one knows his home in this world.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you﴾. Its meaning: if you support the Prophet of Allah or the religion of Allah, He will support you. Support from Allah is protection and guidance. It is reported from Qatadah that he said: "Whoever supports Allah, Allah will support him, and whoever asks Him, He will give to him." It is also said: "He will support you" means by making you prevail over your enemy and elevating you over them.

And His saying: ﴿and make your feet firm﴾, meaning: in fighting. It is also said: He will make your feet firm upon the Sirat (the bridge over Hell). This has been related from Ibn 'Abbas.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve, for them is ruin (ta'san), and He will misguide their deeds﴾ means: far removal (ba'dan) for them. Ta's (ta'san) in the language (lughah) is stumbling and falling. Tha'lab said: ta's is destruction (halak).

Ibn al-Sikkit said: ta's is that one falls on his face, and naks is that one falls on his head.

It is also said: "fata'san lahum" means evil (sharran) for them and perdition (tabban) for them. As for what came in the report (khabar), "ta'isa wa-intakasa" [may he fall and be overturned], we have already explained the meaning of ta'isa. As for the meaning of His saying "intakasa," it means that his affair is reversed and corrupted, and this is in the sense of supplication (du'a').

And His saying: ﴿and He will misguide their deeds﴾ means: Allah will misguide (adalla) their deeds, in the sense of: He will nullify (ahbatha) them. If it is said: What deed do the disbelievers have that Allah the Exalted would nullify? The answer: They used to do deeds seeking the merit of good and drawing near to Allah the Exalted, such as charity (sadaqah), maintaining ties of kinship (silat al-rahim), pilgrimage (hajj), circumambulation (tawaf), and what is similar to that, and they would think that Allah the Exalted would reward them for them. So Allah the Exalted informed that He nullifies them by their disbelief.
That is because they disliked what God sent down, so He caused their deeds to come to nothing. Meaning: they disliked the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and what God sent down of the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them⁠—﴾ meaning: He annihilated them because of their disbelief.

And His saying: ﴿and for the disbelievers there are similar [consequences]﴾ meaning: for these disbelievers there is a similar evil outcome to that of those disbelievers.

And His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Protector (mawla) of those who believe﴾ meaning: the Walī (Protector, Patron) of those who believe. This is also how it is read in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud.

And His saying: ﴿and because the disbelievers have no protector (mawla)﴾ meaning: Allah, may He be exalted, does not take them as allies, in the sense that He does not guide them and does not give them victory. In some reports: 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, asked Ibn al-Kawwa', "Who is the Lord of the worlds?" He said, "Allah." He said, "You have spoken the truth." He said, "Who is the protector (mawla) of the people?" He said, "Allah." He said, "You have lied," and he recited—

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 11:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Protector (mawla) of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no protector (mawla) for them.﴾

It is narrated from Qatadah, who said: "The verse was revealed concerning the battle of Uhud. When killing and wounds spread among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and what was done to the Prophet (ﷺ) was done, the polytheists called out: 'A day for a day of Badr, and war is (a matter of) turns (sijal).' Then they said: 'We have al-'Uzza, and you have no al-'Uzza.' So he (ﷺ) said: 'Say: Allah is our Protector (mawlana), and you have no protector, and they are not equal: our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire.'"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. But those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat﴾. He means: they do not fear punishment, and they do not hope for reward. And it was said: their only concern is enjoyment and eating, like cattle.

And His saying: ﴿And the Fire is their abode﴾, i.e., their dwelling place.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And how many a town﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin min qaryah" (wa-ka'in min qaryah), with the lightened pronunciation.

Al-Akhfash recited the verse of Labid:

(And how many a king have we seen, and a commoner, and the key of the shackle for the bound prisoner)

Its meaning: how many people of a town were stronger than the people of your town which expelled you, that is, its people expelled you.

And His words: ﴿We destroyed them, and there was none to help them﴾ — that is, there was no one among them to prevent them from Our punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is he who is upon clear evidence from his Lord﴾, i.e., upon certainty concerning the matter of his Lord.

It is also said: the intended meaning of the verse is Muhammad.

As for His saying: ﴿like one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him﴾, it is Abu Jahl. It is also said: the verse concerns all the believers and the disbelievers. The meaning of the verse is that the two groups are not equal, so the (second half) is omitted for the understanding of the addressee. This is like a man who says: "Whoever does good deeds is happy, and whoever does evil deeds is wretched." Then he says: "Is the one who is happy like the one who is [wretched]?", meaning: it cannot be, and the (answer) is omitted for the understanding of the addressee. It is also said: the alif in His saying ﴿Is he (afaman)﴾ is an alif of interrogation and confirmation regarding what the addressee already knows from it.

As for His saying: ﴿and follow their desires﴾, i.e., they followed their desires in adopting disbelief.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 15:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿The likeness of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised﴾. In the reading of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him): "The examples (amthāl) of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised." The meaning is: the description (ṣifa) of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised, that is, the attributes (ṣifāt) of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised. Its meaning is: promised to the God-fearing who avoided (al-shirk) [polytheism].

And His words: ﴿Therein are rivers of water unaltered (ghayr āsin)﴾, that is, not changing. It is said: the water became āsin (ya’sin) when it changed, and ajana (ya’jan) when it changed as well. He said this because water changes with long standing, whereas the water of the Garden does not change with long standing.

And His words: ﴿and rivers of milk, its taste unchanging﴾, that is, it does not turn sour. He said this because milk, when time passes over it, changes and turns sour. It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I was brought two vessels on the night of the Mi‘raj: in one was wine and in the other milk. I took the milk and drank it, and Jibril (peace be upon him) said: 'You have chosen the fitrah.'"

It is also well known that "the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he ate food, would thank Allah the Exalted and ask Him to provide him with something better than it, except for milk: when he drank milk, he would thank Allah the Exalted and would not say, 'Provide us with something better than it.'"

And His words: ﴿and rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾. Delight (al-ladhdha): the contentment of the soul in drinking. We have already explained the description of the wine of the Garden before this.

And His words: ﴿and rivers of honey, purified﴾, that is, cleansed of impurities and dregs.

It is also said: purified of wax, so that there is no wax in it.

And His words: ﴿and for them therein of every fruit﴾, that is, the fruits.

And His words: ﴿and forgiveness from their Lord﴾, that is, pardon from their Lord.

And His words: ﴿Is it like one who abides forever in the Fire﴾, that is, whoever is given such bounties, his state is like the state of one who abides forever in the Fire.

And His words: ﴿and they are given to drink boiling water (ḥamīm)﴾. Ḥamīm: it is water that has reached the utmost of heat. In the exegesis it is said that it is water over which the fires of Jahannam have been kindled since it was created; when the disbeliever brings it near his face to drink, it roasts his face, and the skin of his face and the scalp fall off.

﴿They say to those who were given knowledge: "What did he say just now?" Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, and who follow their desires.﴾

In some chains (masānīd), on the narration of Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī, that the Prophet said: "When the disbeliever drinks the ḥamīm, it cuts his intestines, so that they come out from his anus," and then he recited the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and they are given to drink boiling water, and it cuts their intestines to pieces.﴾

In some reports from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbaydillāh al-Kātib, he said: "I returned from Makkah and passed by Ṭīzanābādh, a place between Kufa and Baghdad, and I saw a vineyard with abundant grapes. I recalled the words of Abū Nuwās:

(At Ṭīzanābādh, I passed by no vineyard
without marveling at one who drinks water.)

Then I heard a speaker saying, whose voice I heard but whom I did not see:

(In the Blazing Fire is a ḥamīm that he who gulps it,
a created being, will have his intestines left in his belly.)"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 16:

The Almighty's words: ﴿And among them are some who listen to you﴾ meaning: and among the disbelievers are some who listen to you, i.e., listen to what you say.

And His words: ﴿until, when they leave you, they say to those who were given knowledge﴾. Abdullah ibn Buraydah and a group said: it is Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. It is also said that it is Abu al-Darda'. There is another view regarding the verse: that it refers to all the Companions of the Messenger of Allah.

And His words: ﴿"What did he say just now?"﴾ i.e., what did your companion just say now? "Just now" (ānifan) means: recently. They would say this in a mocking manner, meaning: we were occupied and did not listen to his speech, so what did he say?

And His words: ﴿These are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed﴾ i.e., Allah has sealed their hearts, and did not guide them to accept the word of His Messenger. Ibn al-A'rabi said: the sealing upon the heart is (from) understanding the speech.

And His words: ﴿and have followed their own desires﴾ i.e., their own whims. The purpose and benefit of the verse is: to prevent the Muslims from being like these people, and to explain their state to the believers.

"The Almighty's saying: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾ means: He increases them in clarification and right direction. It is also said: He increases them in guidance, meaning acting upon the abrogating ruling (nasikh) after acting upon the abrogated ruling (mansukh). And it is said: taking up the firm obligations ('aza'im) after acting upon the concessions (rukhas).

And His saying: ﴿and gives them their taqwa﴾ means: the reward of their taqwa (God-consciousness)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they then await anything but the Hour?﴾ That is: do they await anything but the Hour coming upon them suddenly, that is, coming to them unexpectedly.

And His saying: ﴿Its signs have already come.﴾ That is, its signs (ashrat, sing. shart, "sign" or "portent"). In the exegesis it is said that His saying ﴿Its signs have already come﴾ refers to Muhammad. It has been narrated from him (ﷺ) that he said: "I was sent while the Hour is like these two," and he pointed to the index finger and the middle finger, "and it has outstripped it just as this one has outstripped that." In another narration: "It almost outstripped me." The reports have differed concerning the first of the signs of the Hour. According to some reports: "The first of the signs of the Hour is the rising of the sun from its west, and at that time the door of repentance will be closed, and ﴿no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before﴾, as God the Exalted has said." In another report: "The first of the signs of the Hour is a fire that will emerge from the east and drive the people toward the west." It is also said: "Its first sign is the emergence of the beast." In the reports: [that] these signs will occur within a short period, and some of them will follow one another in succession. It has also been said: "like the pearls of a necklace when its string breaks, one following another."

And His saying: ﴿How then for them, when their reminder comes to them?﴾ Its meaning: where then is their escape and refuge when there comes to them that which reminds them? That is, when they witness the matter and these signs are present. Qatadah said its meaning is: "How for them, when there comes to them" – that is, the Hour – "their reminder?" That is: how for them is the benefit of remembrance? That is, the benefit of remembrance, were they to seek it when the Hour comes upon them; and the intended meaning is the loss of the benefit of remembrance at the presence of the matter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah﴾. If it is said: How does He say "So know that there is no deity except Allah," when he already knows it? The answer has two aspects. The first: what is meant is steadfastness upon knowledge, not the beginning of knowledge. The second: its meaning is "So remember that there is no deity except Allah," and knowledge is expressed by remembrance (dhikr) because it occurs to him. It is also said: the address is to the Messenger, but what is meant is his community (ummah).

His saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin, and for the believing men and believing women﴾. It is established by the narration of al-Zuhri from Abu Salamah from Abu Hurairah that the Prophet said: "Indeed I seek forgiveness from Allah seventy times a day," and in another narration: "a hundred times."

If it is said: How did He command him to seek forgiveness when he was protected from sins (ma'sum)? The answer: he was not free from error, slips, and some minor sins, so Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to seek forgiveness for them, and He commanded him to seek forgiveness for the believing men and believing women, and he would supplicate for them and seek forgiveness for them.

In the well-known report: when the illness in which he died began, the Prophet went out to Uhud, sought forgiveness for the martyrs of Uhud, then sought forgiveness for the believing men and believing women... and the report in it is lengthy.

His saying: ﴿And Allah knows your movement and your resting place﴾. That is: your turning about (munqalab) and the place of your stay. It is also said: "your movement" refers to by day, and "your resting place" to by night. It was said: "your movement and your resting place" means He knows everything you are upon in all your states. It is also said: "He knows your movement" means your going about in this world, and "your resting place" means your final return in the Hereafter, whether to Paradise or to the Fire. It is established by the narration of Humran from Uthman that the Messenger of Allah said: "Whoever dies knowing that there is no deity except Allah enters Paradise." ﴿Those who believe say: "Why was a surah not sent down?"﴾ But when a decisive (muhkamah) surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned in it, you see those in whose hearts is disease...

And on the authority of Ubayd ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said: [regarding] His saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin, and for the believing men and believing women﴾ — then he said: I was a man sharp of tongue toward my family, so I said: O Messenger of Allah, I fear my tongue will cause me to enter the Fire. He said: "Where are you in regard to seeking forgiveness? Indeed I seek forgiveness from Allah a hundred times a day." In some reports from the Prophet it is related that he said: "The best deed is there is no deity except Allah, and the best supplication is I seek forgiveness from Allah." In some reports: "When a man seeks forgiveness for the believing men and believing women, Allah, exalted is He, returns to him for every believing man and woman."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been sent down?"﴾ That is: "Why has a surah not been sent down?" It is said in the tafsir that they used to take comfort in revelation when it descended, and they would be slow to accept it when it was delayed.

His saying: ﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down﴾ In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is "muhdathah" (newly revealed). Regarding His saying ﴿decisive (muhkamah)﴾ there are two interpretations. The first: muhkamah means decisive by the mention of jihad and fighting against the disbelievers, and jihad and fighting are the most burdensome of commands upon the self.

The second interpretation: muhkamah means decisive in its commands and prohibitions.

His saying: ﴿you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ That is, hypocrisy. If it is asked: how can He speak of the believers at the beginning of the verse and then say ﴿you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, who are the hypocrites, and a hypocrite is not a believer? The answer: there is an ellipsis in the verse, and its meaning is: "When a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned in it, the believers rejoice and take comfort in it." And ﴿you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the gaze of one overcome by death﴾ means: they fixed their eyes upon you and looked intently, likening the fixed gaze to the gaze at the time of death. Such a state befell them because, if they fought, they feared destruction, and if they did not fight, they feared the exposure of their hypocrisy.

The verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Rifa'ah ibn al-Harith, and the rest of the hypocrites.

His saying: ﴿So woe to them (fa-awla lahum)﴾ This is a warning and a threat. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is for those who disliked it. The Arabs say to one who has come near to ruin and escaped: "Awla laka" (woe to you / closer to destruction for you), meaning a warning to him against the like of that. It is reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah that whenever a dead person was in his vicinity (aqwatihi), that is, near him, he would say to himself: "Awla laka, you were nearly the one who is cut off (al-sawad al-mukhtarim)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 21:

As for His words, ﴿Obedience and honourable speech﴾, there are several opinions regarding it. The first: it is in the sense of a command, and its meaning is: say, "We believe; obedience and honourable speech." The honourable speech (al-qawl al-ma'ruf) is responding by hearing and obeying.

The second opinion: His words ﴿Obedience and honourable speech﴾ mean: obedience and honourable speech are better and more pleasing for them.

The third opinion: this is a report from them before the revelation of the verse of fighting; they used to say it in this manner, but when the verse of fighting was revealed, they disliked it and grew distressed. It is also said that His words ﴿Obedience and honourable speech﴾ are a parenthetical interjection within the connected discourse preceding it.

As for His words ﴿But when the matter is resolved upon, then if they had been true to Allah, it would have been better for them﴾, the meaning of ﴿when the matter is resolved upon﴾ is: the matter became serious and the obligation of fighting became binding. ﴿Then if they had been true to Allah﴾ means: if they had fulfilled what they had pledged to Allah of jihad, and had met Allah's command with compliance, it would have been better for them.

"The words of the Exalted: ﴿Then, if you were to turn away, would you perhaps cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?﴾ Regarding this there are two views. The first: "if you turn away" means if you were to hold authority (wilayah), i.e., if authority were yours. The second: "if you turn away" means if you turn away from belief in the Messenger and in the Qur'an, i.e., you turn aside; so will there be from you anything other than that you cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? It was also said, according to the first view, that this occurred in the early period of Islam: when the Quraysh took over the affair, they caused corruption in the land and severed the ties of kinship, and that was the killing of the Quraysh by the Banu Hashim and the killing of the Banu Hashim by the Quraysh."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 23:

And His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed﴾, meaning: Allah has expelled them (from His mercy).

And His saying: ﴿and deafened them and blinded their vision﴾, meaning: He made them like the deaf, and (He made them) like the blind.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 24:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ Tadabbur (reflection) is thinking and considering what the outcome of a matter will lead to.

As for His words: ﴿Or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾, its meaning is: "Rather, there are locks upon their hearts." It is by way of metaphor (majaz), so the lock is mentioned to signify the closing of the heart against understanding the Qur'an. In the tafsir it is related: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was reciting this verse to a young man, and that young man said: 'Rather, there are locks upon the hearts until Allah opens them.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: 'You have spoken the truth.'"

And it is related from some of them: "[It is] like an iron lock upon the door."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 25:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them﴾. Al-huda (guidance) is the clarification that leads to the truth.

And His saying: ﴿Satan made it seem fair to them﴾, meaning: he adorned it for them.

And His saying: ﴿and He gave them respite﴾, meaning: He granted them time by extending their lifespan for them. It refers back to Allah, the Exalted, and its meaning is: Allah, the Exalted, gave them respite. It was also recited as "wa-umlā lahum" in the passive voice (with its subject unnamed), and it was recited irregularly (shādhdh) as "wa-umlī lahum" with the yā' sukūn (sukūn on the yā'), meaning: "and I give them respite."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 26:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿That is because they said to those who hated what Allah has sent down﴾. Regarding this verse there are two opinions. The first: it is the saying of the Jews to the hypocrites. The Jews said to the hypocrites: "We will obey you in some of the matter," i.e., in concealing the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), while we know that he is a Messenger. The second opinion, and it is the more apparent, is that it is the saying of the hypocrites to the Jews.

And His saying: ﴿those who hated what Allah has sent down﴾ refers to the Jews, and they hated it out of envy and transgression.

And His saying: ﴿We will obey you in some of the matter﴾ means: in opposition to Muhammad (ﷺ) and enmity toward him.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah knows their secrets﴾ means: what some of them confided to others. This opinion is preferable, because the preceding verses are about the hypocrites.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 27:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So how will it be when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?﴾ That is: they strike their faces at the time of death with the sheets of disbelief. It was also said: this refers to the Day of Resurrection.

And His words: ﴿and their backs﴾ mean: they strike their backs when driving them towards the Fire, and this is on the Day of Resurrection. In some tafsirs: there is no disobedient person who dies except that the angels strike his face and his back when they place him in the grave.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because they followed what angered God and disliked His pleasure, so He nullified their deeds﴾. "Nullified" means "made void"; we have already explained its meaning earlier.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 29:

The Most High said: ﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will never bring out their malice?﴾ Al-adghan (malice): the plural of dghn (ḍaghn), which means resentment, enmity, and deceit. The meaning of the verse is: do the hypocrites and the disbelievers think that what is in their hearts toward His Messenger and toward the believers will never become apparent?

The poet said about ḍaghn:

(Say to Abu Hind: what did you intend with speech... it was bad for the friend, and it blackened the malice) That is: the grudges.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 30:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you﴾, meaning: We would have made you recognise them.

And His saying: ﴿So you would have recognised them by their mark﴾, meaning: We would have placed upon their faces a mark by which you would know them.

And His saying: ﴿And you will surely know them by the tone of speech﴾, meaning: in the import of the speech, its purport and its intended meaning. It is related from some of them: a person's speech and action are evidence of his intention. It is said: "laḥn" in speech means deviating from what is correct. The laḥn here is speech whereby the listener understands its meaning while the speaker keeps his intended meaning hidden within it. The poet said:

(His speech is sound, yet at times he speaks with laḥn ... and the best speech is that which is laḥ)

In the well-known report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You bring your disputes before me, and perhaps some of you is more eloquent (alḥan) in his argument than another," meaning: more perceptive (afṭan). It is related from some of them: I am amazed at the one who recognises the laḥn of speech, how he can lie. In the tafsir it is mentioned: after this verse, no hypocrite remained hidden from the Messenger of Allah, and he would recognise them by the tone of their speech.

And the Exalted's saying: ﴿And Allah knows your deeds﴾, meaning: those which you do.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 31:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and are patient﴾. That is, We will know with the knowledge of witnessing (ʿilm al-shahada), which is the knowledge upon which reward and punishment are based. It is also said: [We shall deal with you] in the manner of one who wishes to know your deeds. And it is said its meaning is: until you know that We have known your deeds.

As for His words: ﴿and the patient, and We will test your reports﴾. That is, We will know the patient, and We will know your reports. Mujahid, when he reached this verse, would say: "O Allah, we ask You not to test our reports, for we would be disgraced."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and hindered [others] from the way of Allah﴾ — meaning: they prevented people from faith in Allah.

And His saying: ﴿and opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them﴾ — meaning: they opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them.

And His saying: ﴿they will not harm Allah at all﴾ — meaning: they will not diminish anything of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿and He will render their deeds void﴾ — meaning: He will nullify their deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 33:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not render your deeds void﴾. From Abu al-'Aliya al-Riyahi, who said: They (i.e., the Companions) used to say: "No harm will come with faith, just as no benefit comes with disbelief," until Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿and do not render your deeds void﴾ through doubt and hypocrisy. It is also said: through deceit and treachery, and through (committing) major sins.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar others from the way of Allah, and then die while they are disbelievers, Allah will never forgive them.﴾ Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 35:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace﴾, meaning: (do not become feeble).

And His saying: ﴿and call to peace﴾, meaning: to reconciliation (al-sulh). God the Exalted forbade the Muslims to seek reconciliation with the disbelievers when they are able to fight.

And His saying: ﴿while you are the superior ones﴾, meaning: the victorious, the dominant.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and God is with you﴾, meaning: with help and protection.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾, meaning: He will not diminish anything of the reward of your deeds. And it has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no hour that passes over the Muslim servant in which he does not remember God, except that it will be a tirah (deficiency) against him on the Day of Resurrection," meaning: a loss.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the life of this world is but amusement and diversion﴾, meaning: that which is diverted with and played with.

And His saying: ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth﴾. Concerning this there are several opinions. The first: "And He will not ask you for all your wealth; He only asks you for the amount of zakat, which is well known." The second opinion: "He does not ask you for your wealth for His own sake; He asks it only for your sake." The third opinion: "And He will not ask you for your wealth, because in reality it is not yours; it belongs to Him."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 37:

And the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy﴾. That is, He exaggerates in asking you, and it is said: He insists upon you and presses you hard. In some of the proverbs of the Arabs: "The one who asks insistently is not like the one who is denied" (the fifth [proverb]).

And in some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah loves the modest, the chaste, and dislikes the importunate beggar who presses his request."

His words ﴿you would be stingy﴾: that is, you would withhold.

And his words: ﴿and He would bring out your rancor﴾: that is, the pressing would bring out your rancor, and make manifest what is in your inner selves of stinginess, withholding, hypocrisy and doubt. And in some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Tell the person about his hatred" (akhbir taqlahu), meaning: inform the person of your hatred for him. And from some of them, he said: "Aqlahu bi-khabar," meaning: "I hate him," so he is the one who tests. And in some anecdotes, Mukhariq sang for al-Ma'mun:

(I am longing for the shade of a companion, who is gentle and clear, if I become turbid toward him)

So al-Ma'mun said: "Take the caliphate from me and bring me this companion."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 47, verse 38:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Here you are, these are they who are invited to spend in the way of Allah﴾, meaning: O you (ya ha'ulaa'), ﴿who are invited to spend in the way of Allah﴾, meaning: in jihad.

And His saying: ﴿Among you is one who is stingy﴾, meaning: who withholds (yamna'). And His saying: ﴿And whoever is stingy, is only stingy against himself﴾, meaning: he forfeits the share of his own soul.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is the Rich, and you are the poor﴾, meaning: He is Rich without you, and you are poor in need of Him.

And His saying: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people﴾, meaning: if you turn away (ta'riduu).

And His saying: ﴿another people other than you﴾. Concerning this there are several views. The first: they are the angels of heaven, and this is the strongest of the views. The second view: "If you turn away, O company of Quraysh, He will replace you with another people," meaning: the people of Yemen, and the Ansar were among them, for the Aws and the Khazraj are two tribes from Yemen. A poet has said:

(And for Allah there are Aws, others, and Khazraj...)

The third view, which is the well-known one: "If you turn away, O company of the Arabs, He will replace you with another people," meaning: the non-Arabs (al-'Ajam). In the well-known report: some people asked the Prophet about the meaning of this verse and said: "Who are those whom He will replace us with?" Salman was sitting beside him, so he said: "This one and his people." Then he said: "Even if the religion were suspended from the Pleiades, men from Persia would reach it."

And His saying: ﴿then they will not be like you﴾, meaning: they will be better than you and more obedient to Me. Its meaning: they will not be like you in opposing the commands. And Allah knows best.
